newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-BEDFORD PREDICTS BEST-EVER LONDON MARATHON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BEDFORD PREDICTS BEST-EVER LONDON MARATHON.

text.p: David Bedford, race director of the London Marathon, believes that Sunday's race could be the best in the event's 16-year history.
"We have assembled what I think are two of the most talented fields ever put together for a marathon," said Bedford, the former 10,000 metres world record holder.
The big attraction in the men's race is Olympic champion Josiah Thugwane and Bedford is known to have spent a considerable amount of his $1 million budget in obtaining the South African's services.

Thugwane is reputed to have been paid $100,000 to run although Bedford refused to name the figure. "We never discuss appearance fees but getting an Olympic champion in the race was a priority," he said.
The South African faces a formidable challenge if he is to score his first victory since Atlanta.
Portugal's Antonio Pinto, winner in London in 1992 and third in 1995, has shown good form recently and will be a threat, as will reigning world half-marathon champion Stefano Baldini of Italy.
British hopes rest with Paul Evans, winner of the Chicago Marathon last October, and Richard Nerurkar, fifth in Atlanta.
The women's race also looks likely to be the most competitive to date.
Briton Liz McColgan won last year and will have to produce another outstanding performance if she is to retain her title.
Reigning world and European champion Manuela Machado of Portugal has all the credentials to win her fourth important marathon.
China also poses a strong threat in Ren Xiujuan.
Ren took the world half-marathon title last October and has won three of her five marathon outings to date despite being only 22.

She has asked for a pacemaker to take her through the halfway mark on world record schedule with the aim of breaking the world best for the classic 42.195-km distance held by Norway's Ingrid Kristiansen.
Kristiansen ran two hours 21 minutes and six seconds in London 12 years ago but none of Sunday's women's field has a best anything close to that.
